Root cause candidate: stale UTC timezone on migrated Incident-only accounts

Confirmed via membership.Users export for Vallarta. This is the same gap flagged on RCS-28065 (Ripp): IANA timezone is only written to the DB via an async ajax call fired from the user's browser on login. Incident-only tenants have no other path to set it, so any account that hasn't logged into the platform since cutover is still sitting on the UTC default written by the migration job.

Data (n=419 total accounts):

  • 308 accounts are TimeZone = UTC; all 308 have LastLoginDate = NULL (no login since migration).

  • 111 accounts show correct local TZ (mostly America/Los_Angeles); all 111 have a populated LastLoginDate.

  • Isolating just the migration batch (CreateDate = 2026-07-30 17:41:06.613, 305 accounts): 287 still UTC, 18 self-corrected after logging in. No accounts outside that pattern.

  • Case owner in the reported example (2026-ADUP-40-96, Fernando Torres) is in the 287: TimeZone = UTC, LastLoginDate = NULL.

This lines up with the reported symptom (alert delayed to the next day / inconsistent timing) — smart alert date-window logic evaluated against a UTC-context record vs. actual PT wall-clock time would explain exactly this behavior.

Requesting the same fix applied for Ahold (RCS-28030) and discussed for Stater Bros: bulk-update TimeZone to America/Los_Angeles in membership.Users for the affected Vallarta accounts, rather than waiting on individual logins to self-correct. Note the STORE HR## / service accounts in that set will never log in through a browser, so they need to be included explicitly — they won't self-heal via the async path.

David Vargas
Support Engineer

Hi Tatiana,

Thank you for the example you provided. We reviewed the change history for case 2026-ADUP-40-96 with our engineering team and wanted to share what we found.

Smart Alerts are triggered when a case is fully saved/completed, not from the date the report was first opened or entered as pending. Looking at the history for this case:

  • The report was first opened/pending on 8/10/2026 at 4:23 PM.

  • It was not saved as a completed case until 8/11/2026 at 12:23 AM — nearly 8 hours later.

Since the alert fires on completion, it went out the morning of 8/11, which lines up with when the case was actually finalized rather than when it was first started. In this instance, the alert worked as intended.

If you run into other cases where the alert doesn't arrive even after the case has been fully completed and saved, please send us those case numbers and we'll take a closer look at those specific examples.

David Vargas
Support Engineer

1. Correction

The explanation we gave the customer on 12 August is wrong. We told her Smart Alerts fire only when a case is fully saved or completed, and that case 2026-ADUP-40-96 worked as intended. Both statements fail against the tenant configuration and against her own attachment.

She was right.

Her report shows the case at Case Stage Pending Report to be Completed, HR Case Status Open, every interview field set to Pending, and the Investigation, Recommendation and Resolution sections empty. The case was never completed. An alert went out anyway.

The customer stated that before the platform move, saving a case triggered the alert regardless of stages marked Pending. That matches the filter exactly. Treat her statement as accurate.

2. Alert configuration - read in production 25 August

The tenant holds 19 Smart Alerts. Three active alerts carry Case Types Complaints, which is the Incident Type of the reported case.

HR Alert 13

Investigation Open - Corporate Employee

Accident_CumulativeInjury Equals '1'

No active filter references completion. Shoplifting_CaseStatus and Shoplifting_Stage both exist as available form fields. Both sit unused.

The first filter reduces:

Shoplifting_DateReported Is not blank\n  AND HRDetail_HR1 Is not blank\n

A value greater than 1 is a value that is present, so the Or collapses into its second term. HRDetail_HR1 holds the narrative body of the complaint. It carries a value whenever someone writes the report.

4. What support cannot determine

Root cause. We hold read access to data. We do not hold code or application logs.

Carry one distinction into the investigation:

RunStatus = Success means the process executed. It does not mean mail reached a recipient. The customer reports alerts not received. Check the send path separately from the evaluation path.

5. Ruled out - do not repeat

Hypothesis

Result

HR1 as the gating variable

Refuted. Zero blanks in either period.

Synchronous evaluation moved to batch

Refuted against DateEntered. One hour share at 40.3% pre and 34.8% post, inside the margin of error for n=112.

Hourly distribution of RunDate

Unusable. 308 of 419 accounts carry a wrong timezone, so the defect contaminates the measurement variable.

6. Still open

Account timezone. 308 of 419 accounts show TimeZone = UTC with LastLoginDate = NULL. ENG-7236 covers this and has sat in Backlog since 13 August. Vallarta never received the remediation applied to Ahold under RCS-28030. Include the STORE HR## service accounts. They never reach the platform through a browser and never self correct.

Timestamps on this tenant. The case record shows Date Case Reported 8/10/2026. The Change History shows the earliest SAVE.CASE at 8/11/2026 12:23 AM on HRFirstReport.aspx, with no event at 4:23 PM on 8/10 across its 23 entries. The two differ by exactly 8 hours, which is UTC minus PST. California ran on PDT, minus 7, in August. Confirm which surface renders UTC and which renders local before quoting any timestamp from this tenant as evidence.

ENG-6612 is not related to this ticket. It covers attachment handling in Cohesion mode, reached Done, and deployed to production on 4 August, one week before this was reported. One exception applies. HR Alert 10 filters on RelatedDoc_AttachmentType and configures Include Attachment Types, so that alert alone depends on the attachment pipeline ENG-6612 touched.

1. Correction

The Aug 25 internal analysis proposed a fixed Pacific offset without DST as the cause of the 8 hour gap between the client's reported time and the Change History display. Today's query results rule that out. The stored value converts correctly to PDT, UTC minus 7, matching the 4:23pm Pacific time the client reported for the same save. The gap comes from the History modal itself, which adds a flat 1 hour to the raw UTC value instead of converting to Pacific.

2. Environment and steps to reproduce

Production. Tenant Vallarta Supermarkets, Client ID 432, database sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-432-vsa-platform.

Vallarta (VSA), case 2026-ADUP-40-96

  1. Open case 2026-ADUP-40-96 in nettrack.

  2. Open Change History from the case menu.

  3. Scroll to the oldest entry, a SAVE.CASE row.

  4. Note the displayed timestamp.

Expected: the displayed timestamp reflects the case record's local Pacific time, a UTC minus 7 conversion from the stored value. Actual: the modal shows 8/11/2026 12:23 AM. The raw incident.CaseChanges.DateChanged value for that row is 2026-08-10 23:23:43.000 UTC. The displayed value equals the raw UTC value plus exactly 1 hour. See attachment image-20260812-181001.png, already on this ticket, uploaded by David Vargas on 2026-08-12, showing the same modal render.

3. Findings

Verified. incident.CaseChanges.DateChanged for the first SAVE.CASE on 2026-ADUP-40-96 is 2026-08-10 23:23:43.000 UTC. Verified. The Change History modal displays this row as 8/11/2026 12:23 AM, exactly raw plus 1 hour. Verified. 2026-08-10 23:23:43 UTC converts correctly to 2026-08-10 16:23:43 Pacific, PDT, UTC minus 7. This matches the 4:23pm Pacific time the client reported for the same save. Verified. Vianney Valdez's account, incident.LPUser2 UserID 32665, carries TimeZone America/Los_Angeles in membership.Users. Her account is not misconfigured. Unverified, from AI triage, listed so it is not re-explored. The modal's plus 1 hour behavior could come from a hardcoded UTC plus 1 fallback in the render path, a common pattern when a server side TimeZoneInfo lookup fails.

4. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

I pulled incident.CaseChanges directly against the production database for tenant 432. incident.ChangeHistory exists in this tenant and holds zero rows, it does not carry this data. I confirmed the real columns with INFORMATION_SCHEMA before writing the query. I compared the raw DateChanged value against the modal's rendered timestamp for the same row, and against the client's independently reported wall clock time.

Claude flagged this as the likely root cause. I checked A, B and C myself, and here is what I found. This is what I think is happening. Could someone else evaluate this and give me your thoughts?

No conversations happened outside this ticket on this finding.

I do not have access to the Change History render code or the server's TimeZoneInfo configuration. Please confirm whether the render path uses a hardcoded offset or a failed TimeZoneInfo lookup.

5. Ruled out. Do not repeat

Fixed Pacific offset without DST as the storage mechanism. Ruled out, the stored UTC value converts correctly with DST applied. Vianney Valdez's account timezone as misconfigured. Ruled out, her account carries the correct IANA zone.

6. Still open

  1. Confirm whether the Change History render path adds a hardcoded 1 hour offset, or falls back to it when a TimeZoneInfo lookup fails.

  2. Confirm whether this render defect affects other tenants or only Vallarta.

  3. This finding is separate from the smart alert trigger timing issue already under review on this ticket. Evaluate it independently, do not combine the two into one fix.
